Title: Earnings Quality and Investor Reaction to Restatement Announcements
							| Advances in Business Research
# Earnings Quality and Investor Reaction to Restatement Announcements. The purpose of this research is to help clarify the ambiguity surrounding market participants’ pricing of earnings quality using one clearly observable indicator of low-quality earnings, accounting restatements. This study examines the effect pre-restatement earnings quality has onshort-window returns following restatement announcements using a cross-section of 719 publicly traded firms that announced restatements between 1997 and 2004. Accrual metrics are used to proxy for earnings quality. Results indicate that the market reaction to restatement announcements is significantly influenced by pre-restatement earnings quality. Specifically, the accrual measure of earnings quality is significantly and negatively related to the market reaction. This finding provides evidence that investors are attune to implications for poor earnings quality communicated by accruals quality and that this awareness is reflected in stock prices prior to the announcement of a clearly observable measure of poor earnings quality, accounting restatements. results.title: Discretionary accrual: Significance and symbolism
results.content: # Significance of Discretionary accrual. Discretionary accrual, as defined in Environmental Sciences, is a component of total accruals. It represents a structure that is difficult to estimate. It is quantified via the magnitude of discretionary accruals. Discretionary accruals are identified by deducting non-discretionary accruals from the total accruals. Furthermore, it is a measure calculated using a specific model and is often used as a control variable in analysis. ## The concept of Discretionary accrual in scientific sources Science Books. Discretionary accruals, a component of total accruals, are difficult to estimate and quantified by deducting non-discretionary accruals. They are calculated using a specific model and serve as a control variable. (1) The absolute value of discretionary accruals is used as a proxy for information quality in measuring information disclosure. (2) Studies have confirmed the effectiveness of systems like the substantial delisting investigation by showing a decrease in discretionary accruals after its implementation.

Title: The Accrual Anomaly: Why Investors Should Care About Accruals Amp; Earnings Quality - Business Insider
# The accrual anomaly: Why investors should care about accruals amp; earnings quality. In order to test out the longstanding view that **investors fixate too heavily on corporate earnings and not on cash generation**, he decided to rank companies based on their quot;accrual ratioquot; for last year's results, i.e the size of non-cash earnings relative to total assets. He then measured how their shares performed in the year after the results were announced, effectively quot;going longquot; the top decile of stocks with the lowest accrual ratio and quot;going shortquot; the bottom decile with the highest accrual ratio. ## **What are Accruals anyway?**. ## **Does Accrual Screening Work?**. As already mentioned, Sloan’s work found that companies with low accrual ratios massively outperform companies with high accrual ratios. A subsequent study in 2006, quot;Cash Flows, Accruals and Future Returnsquot; found that an accrual-based strategy still beat the market by more than 9% a year. They tend to value the earnings of a high accrual company just as highly as the same earnings of a low accrual company, even though the high accrual company’s earnings are more likely to reverse in future years. Similarly, when a low accrual company’s earnings accelerate in future years, they are surprised in a good way and bid up the stock price. A Washington University study looked at this issue and concluded that the accruals effect is concentrated in firms  with high 'idiosyncratic volatility' (i.e. stocks that move all over the place, without regard to market levels), as well as low prices and low volume, making it risky and expensive for arbitrageurs to take positions in such stocks with extreme accruals.
